source_text: Ὁ γνωστικὸς ἄρα τὴν προσεχεστέραν ἀναμάσσεται ὁμοιότητα, τὴν διάνοιαν τὴν τοῦ διδασκάλου, ἥντινα ἐκεῖνος νοῶν ἐνετείλατό τε καὶ συνεβούλευσε τοῖς φρονίμοις καὶ σώφροσι, ταύτην συνιείς, ὡς ὁ διδάξας ἐβούλετο, καὶ ἰδίᾳ τὴν νόησιν ἀναλαβὼν τὴν μεγαλοπρεπῆ, διδάξας μὲν ἀξιολόγως ἐπὶ τῶν δωμάτων τοὺς ὑψηλῶς οἰκοδομεῖσθαι δυναμένους, προκατάρξας δὲ τῆς τῶν λεγομένων ἐνεργείας κατὰ τὸ ὑπόδειγμα τῆς πολιτείας· δυνατὰ γὰρ ἐνετείλατο, καὶ δεῖ τῷ ὄντι ἀρχικὸν εἶναι καὶ ἡγεμονικὸν τὸν βασιλικόν τε καὶ Χριστιανόν, ἐπεὶ μὴ τῶν ἔξω μόνον θηρίων κατακυριεύειν ἐτάγημεν, ἀλλὰ καὶ τῶν ἐν ἡμῖν αὐτοῖς ἀγρίων παθῶν. κατ’ ἐπίστασιν οὖν, ὡς ἔοικεν, τοῦ κακοῦ καὶ ἀγαθοῦ βίου σῴζεται ὁ γνωστικός, πλέον τῶν γραμματέων καὶ Φαρισαίων συνιείς τε καὶ ἐνεργῶν. ἔντεινον καὶ κατευοδοῦ καὶ βασίλευε, ὁ Δαβὶδ γράφει, ἕνεκεν ἀληθείας καὶ πραότητος καὶ δικαιοσύνης, καὶ ὁδηγήσει σε θαυμαστῶς ἡ δεξιά σου, τουτέστιν ὁ κύριος. τίς οὖν σοφὸς καὶ συνήσει ταῦτα; συνετὸς καὶ γνώσεται αὐτά; διότι εὐθεῖαι αἱ ὁδοὶ τοῦ κυρίου, φησὶν ὁ προφήτης, δηλῶν μόνον δύνασθαι τὸν γνωστικὸν τὰ ἐπικεκρυμμένως πρὸς τοῦ πνεύματος εἰρημένα νοήσειν τε καὶ διασαφήσειν· καὶ ὁ συνίων ἐν τῷ καιρῷ ἐκείνῳ ἐκείνῳ σιωπήσεται, λέγει ἡ γραφή, δηλονότι πρὸς τοὺς ἀναξίους ἐξειπεῖν, ὅτι φησὶν ὁ κύριος· ὁ ἔχων ὦτα ἀκούειν ἀκουέτω, οὐ πάντων εἶναι τὸ ἀκούειν καὶ συνιέναι λέγων. αὐτίκα ὁ Δαβὶδ σκοτεινὸν ὕδωρ ἐν νεφέλαις ἀέρων γράφει· ἀπὸ τῆς τηλαυγήσεως ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ αἱ νεφέλαι διῆλθον, χάλαζα καὶ ἄνθρακες πυρός, ἐπικεκρυμμένους τοὺς ἁγίους λόγους εἶναι διδάσκων. καὶ δὴ τοῖς μὲν γνωστικοῖς διειδεῖς καὶ τηλαυγεῖς καθάπερ χάλαζαν ἀβλαβῆ καταπέμπεσθαι θεόθεν μηνύει, σκοτεινοὺς δὲ τοῖς πολλοῖς καθάπερ τοὺς ἐκ πυρὸς ἀπεσβεσμένους ἄνθρακας, οὓς εἰ μή τις ἀνάψαι καὶ ἀναζωπυρήσαι, οὐκ ἐκφλεγήσονται οὐδ’ ἐμφωτισθήσονται. κύριος, οὖν φησι, δίδωσί μοι γλῶσσαν παιδείας τοῦ γνῶναι ἐν καιρῷ, ἡνίκα δεῖ εἰπεῖν λόγον, οὐ κατὰ τὸ μαρτύριον μόνον, ἀλλὰ γὰρ καὶ τὸν κατ’ ἐρώτησιν καὶ ἀπόκρισιν· καὶ ἡ παιδεία κυρίου ἀνοίγει μου τὸ στόμα. γνωστικοῦ ἄρα καὶ τὸ εἰδέναι χρῆσθαι τῷ λόγῳ καὶ ὁπότε καὶ ὅπως καὶ πρὸς οὕστινας.
pass_a_gloss: The Gnostic then meditates on the nearest likeness, the mind of the Teacher, which He, perceiving, commanded and advised the prudent and self-controlled, this one understanding, as the Teacher wished, and having taken up the great and majestic notion, having taught worthily those who are able to be built up highly, having begun the activity of the things said according to the model of the polity. For He commanded powerful things, and it is necessary for the one who is to be archaic and hegemonic, the royal and Christian, since we were not ordered to rule only over the external beasts, but also over the wild passions within ourselves. Therefore, the Gnostic is saved, knowing the bad and good life, more than the scribes and Pharisees, understanding and acting. David writes, 'Be intent, and proceed, and reign, for the sake of truth and gentleness and righteousness,' and 'the right hand of the Lord will guide you wonderfully,' that is, the Lord. Who then is wise and will understand these things? Will the intelligent one know them? Because the ways of the Lord are straight, the prophet says, showing that only the Gnostic can understand and explain the things said secretly by the Spirit. And the one who understands will be silent at that time, the Scripture says, clearly to those who are unworthy to speak, because the Lord says, 'The one who has ears to hear, let him hear,' not saying that hearing and understanding are for everyone. Immediately, David writes, 'Dark water in clouds of air,' teaching that the holy words are hidden. From the distance before Him, the clouds passed, hail and coals of fire, showing that the Gnostic words are sent down from God like harmless hail to the Gnostics, but to the many, they are like coals extinguished from fire, which, if someone does not ignite and rekindle, will not be inflamed or enlightened. The Lord, therefore, gives me a tongue of education to know in time when it is necessary to speak a word, not only according to testimony, but also according to question and answer. And the education of the Lord opens my mouth. Therefore, it is also necessary for the Gnostic to know how to use the word, and when, and how, and to whom.

pass_b_english: The Gnostic then meditates on the nearest likeness — the mind of the Teacher. The Teacher, perceiving it, commanded and advised the prudent and self-controlled, and the Gnostic understands it exactly as the Teacher wished. Having taken up the majestic notion, he teaches worthily those who can be built up on high, and he begins the activity of the things said according to the model of the polity. For the Teacher commanded powerful things, and it is necessary for the one who is to be archaic and hegemonic — the royal and Christian — to be so, since we were ordered not only to rule over the external beasts but also over the wild passions within ourselves. Therefore the Gnostic is saved, knowing the bad and good life, understanding and acting more than the scribes and Pharisees. David writes, "Be intent, and proceed, and reign, for the sake of truth and gentleness and righteousness" (Psalm 118:106), and "the right hand of the Lord will guide you wonderfully" (Psalm 118:107), that is, the Lord. Who then is wise and will understand these things? Will the intelligent one know them? Because the ways of the Lord are straight, the prophet says, showing that only the Gnostic can understand and explain the things said secretly by the Spirit. And the one who understands will be silent at that time, the Scripture says, clearly to those who are unworthy to speak, because the Lord says, "The one who has ears to hear, let him hear" (Matthew 11:15), not saying that hearing and understanding are for everyone. Immediately David writes, "Dark water in clouds of air," teaching that the holy words are hidden. From the brightness before Him the clouds passed, hail and coals of fire, showing that the Gnostic words are sent down from God like harmless hail to the Gnostics, but to the many they are like coals extinguished from fire, which, if someone does not ignite and rekindle them, will not be inflamed or enlightened. The Lord, therefore, gives me a tongue of education to know in time when it is necessary to speak a word, not only according to testimony but also according to question and answer. And the education of the Lord opens my mouth. Therefore it is also necessary for the Gnostic to know how to use the word, and when, and how, and to whom.
